UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA ALEXANDRIA DIVISION

MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,

Plaintiff,  v.  KATIE HALL, individually; NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN; META PLATFORMS, INC.; and JOHN/JANE DOES 1–6,

Defendants. ____________________________________/

Case No. 1:26-cv-02331

PLAINTIFF’S RULE 54(b) MOTION TO VACATE ECF NO. 96 AND DETERMINE MAGISTRATE JUDGE DAVIS’S OWNERSHIP OF META COMMON STOCK

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine moves under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 54(b) to vacate the Order entered October 22, 2026 (ECF No. 96), which denied ECF No. 86 as moot. Plaintiff seeks restoration, for decision, of the historical financial-interest determination requested in Part V and Request A2 of ECF No. 86. Plaintiff moves for a finding that Magistrate Judge Ivan D. Davis owned common stock of Defendant Meta Platforms, Inc. (“Meta”) on September 9, 2026, when he entered ECF No. 64, and on October 7, 2026, when he entered ECF No. 84. Plaintiff requests determination of the ownership and holding-arrangement facts necessary to apply 28 U.S.C. § 455(d)(4). In the alternative, Plaintiff requests an on-record determination of who owned the reported asset on each date and whether the interest fell within § 455(d)(4), after the factual development necessary to decide that question. A Memorandum in Support accompanies this Motion under Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1). Plaintiff incorporates it by reference.

I.	THE ORDER CHALLENGED

1.	ECF No. 96 denied ECF No. 86 in its entirety. Its operative text reads: “ORDERED that Plaintiff’s Motion is DENIED AS MOOT. The case has been reassigned to Magistrate Judge William E. Fitzpatrick.” ECF No. 96 at 1. Magistrate Judge Davis signed it. It was entered October 22, 2026.

2.	An unnumbered docket entry of the same date reads: “Case Reassigned to Magistrate Judge William E. Fitzpatrick. Magistrate Judge Ivan D. Davis no longer assigned to the case.”

3.	ECF No. 96 states one ground: reassignment. It does not determine whether the asset reported as “FB common stock” is Meta common stock. It does not determine whether that asset was owned on any date in 2026. It does not determine the arrangement through which the asset is held. It does not determine whether any divestiture occurred. It makes no finding on any item in ECF No. 86, Part V.

4.	ECF No. 96 is an interlocutory order. No judgment has been entered. Under Rule 54(b), an order that adjudicates fewer than all the claims “may be revised at any time before the entry of a judgment adjudicating all the claims and all the parties’ rights and liabilities.” Fed. R. Civ. P. 54(b).

II.	THE REQUEST TO BE RESTORED

5.	ECF No. 86 was filed October 13, 2026 and entered October 14, 2026. It presented two kinds of requests.

6.	The first kind was prospective. Request A1 sought disqualification of Magistrate Judge Davis. Request A3 sought determination of the motion before further substantive action. Request A4 sought transfer of the referred matters upon disqualification. ECF No. 86 at 5–6 (Part VII).

7.	The second kind was historical. Part V asked the Court to “state on the record” five facts: “(a) whether the asset reported as ‘FB common stock’ on Exhibits A and B is common stock of Meta Platforms, Inc.; (b) whether that interest was held on July 30, 2026, and on each date on which ECF Nos. 62, 63, 64, 65, 82, and 84 were entered; (c) the date and manner of any divestiture; (d) whether the interest is held directly or through a mutual or common investment fund within the meaning of 28 U.S.C. § 455(d)(4)(i); and (e) any other fact the Court considers material to the application of 28 U.S.C. § 455(f).” ECF No. 86 at 4. Request A2 asked the Court to “[s]tate on the record whether the reported interest was held during the challenged participation, the date and manner of any divestiture, and the facts necessary to determine any claimed exception under 28 U.S.C. § 455(f).” ECF No. 86 at 6.

8.	Reassignment answered the first kind of request. Magistrate Judge Davis no longer participates in this action. Plaintiff does not seek his disqualification from further participation. Plaintiff does not seek his reinstatement. Plaintiff raises no objection to Magistrate Judge Fitzpatrick personally. The separately pending challenge to the source and procedure of the successor designation, ECF Nos. 97–99, is maintained and is addressed in Part VI below.

9.	Reassignment did not answer the second kind. Ownership on September 9, 2026 and on October 7, 2026 is a fact about two judicial acts already completed. The identity of the officer who handles later matters does not change that fact.

10.	This Motion seeks restoration of the second kind of request as to two dates. September 9, 2026 is the date ECF No. 64 was entered. ECF No. 64 required a redline against the original Complaint by September 11, 2026. October 7, 2026 is the date ECF No. 84 was entered. ECF No. 84 denied ECF No. 59 for noncompliance with ECF No. 64. It denied ECF No. 15, which sought discovery from Defendant National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (“NCMEC”), and ECF No. 54, which sought discovery from Meta. ECF No. 84 at 1–2. The Part V requests concerning the dates of ECF Nos. 62, 63, 65, and 82 remain presented in the applications identified in Part VI below. This Motion does not expand them.

III.	GROUNDS FOR RECONSIDERATION

11.	A court may revise an interlocutory order under the same circumstances in which it may depart from the law of the case: “a subsequent trial produc[ing] substantially different evidence,” a change in applicable law, or “clear error causing ‘manifest injustice.’” Carlson v. Boston Scientific Corp., 856 F.3d 320, 325 (4th Cir. 2017). Plaintiff invokes the third ground.

12.	The error. ECF No. 96 treated reassignment as disposing of the entire motion. Reassignment disposed of the prospective requests. It did not reach the historical requests. A request becomes moot when no effectual relief can follow from granting it. Church of Scientology of Cal. v. United States, 506 U.S. 9, 12 (1992). The historical determination requested in ECF No. 86 can still produce effectual relief. It is the factual predicate of Plaintiff’s pending application for relief from ECF Nos. 64 and 84. ECF No. 93 ¶¶ 5, 10(R2), 10(R7). A change in the officer assigned to future matters did not make the request to determine that predicate moot.

13.	The injustice. ECF No. 96 closed the proceeding in which Plaintiff expressly requested determination of the reported financial interest. It did so without deciding ownership or providing for development of the ownership record. ECF Nos. 64 and 84 remain operative, and ECF No. 93 presents a statutory challenge to those orders. Plaintiff contends that terminating the supported historical inquiry as moot, while its subject remains material to that pending challenge, causes manifest injustice. The pending district-judge applications preserve additional means of correction; they do not supply the determination requested in ECF No. 86.

14.	Plaintiff does not present the financial disclosure reports as new evidence. They were before the Court when ECF No. 96 issued. ECF Nos. 86-2, 86-3. The ground is error in the legal effect given to reassignment.

15.	ECF No. 96 made a legal determination that reassignment rendered ECF No. 86 moot in its entirety. Plaintiff asks the successor magistrate judge to reconsider that determination under Rule 54(b). Plaintiff contends that the blanket mootness disposition constitutes clear error causing manifest injustice for the reasons stated here and in the accompanying Memorandum. The requested reconsideration does not require reweighing a prior ownership finding because no such finding was made.

16.	Authority. This Motion is presented within the existing referral of pretrial matters under 28 U.S.C. § 636(b)(1)(A) and Local Civil Rule 72. It asks the assigned magistrate judge to revise an interlocutory pretrial order entered in that referral. It does not invoke 28 U.S.C. § 636(c). By invoking Rule 54(b), Plaintiff does not concede that ECF No. 96 was entered with authority. Plaintiff maintains in ECF Nos. 97–99 the objection that the reassignment may have ended Magistrate Judge Davis’s authority to adjudicate ECF No. 86 before ECF No. 96 was entered. Seeking reconsideration here does not abandon that objection. The two requests are alternatives. If ECF No. 96 was entered without authority, the District Judge may vacate it on that ground. If it was entered with authority, it is an interlocutory order that the assigned magistrate judge may revise under Rule 54(b).

IV.	THE FINDINGS REQUESTED

17.	Plaintiff requests that the Court find:

(a)	The asset reported as “FB common stock” at Part VII, line 6, of the Financial Disclosure Reports at ECF No. 86-2 at 3 (report page 2) and ECF No. 86-3 at 5 (report page 4) is common stock of Meta Platforms, Inc.

(b)	Magistrate Judge Davis owned that stock on September 9, 2026, when he entered ECF No. 64.

(c)	Magistrate Judge Davis owned that stock on October 7, 2026, when he entered ECF No. 84.

(d)	That ownership was a “financial interest” within 28 U.S.C. § 455(d)(4) and was not excluded by § 455(d)(4)(i).

18.	These are findings Plaintiff asks the Court to make. No prior order has made them. The evidentiary basis is stated in the Memorandum in Support. The same asset appears in two consecutive annual reports. Each report describes it as common stock. Each report places it in the same value range, $15,001 to $50,000. Neither report records a transaction on that line during its reporting period. ECF No. 86-2 at 3; ECF No. 86-3 at 5. The reports document the reported holding at the close of 2024 and at the close of 2025. They do not directly document ownership on September 9 or October 7, 2026. Plaintiff requests a finding of continued ownership from that evidence and, to the extent necessary, completion of the record supporting that finding.

19.	The requested findings are confined to ownership and statutory classification. They do not determine knowledge under § 455(b)(4), the application of § 455(f), or the remedy for any order entered. Those questions are presented in ECF No. 93. They are not requested here.

V.	THE ALTERNATIVE REQUEST FOR DETERMINATION AFTER FACTUAL DEVELOPMENT

20.	Alternatively, Plaintiff requests an on-record determination whether the reported asset was owned on September 9 and October 7, 2026, by Magistrate Judge Davis or another holder covered by § 455(b)(4), and whether the interest fell within § 455(d)(4). Plaintiff requests the factual development necessary to decide that question and an opportunity to address the resulting record. This alternative request does not depend on the Court accepting Plaintiff’s inference of continued personal ownership.

21.	The record to be developed is confined to four facts: the issuer and the actual owner of the reported asset; ownership on September 9, 2026 and on October 7, 2026, each date separately; the arrangement through which the asset is held, for purposes of § 455(d)(4)(i); and any disposition of the asset necessary to explain ownership on either date. If the record shows that the asset was owned on either date not by Magistrate Judge Davis individually but by Magistrate Judge Davis as a fiduciary, by his spouse, or by a minor child residing in his household, Plaintiff requests that finding in place of findings (b) and (c). Identification of the holder does not itself determine knowledge under § 455(b)(4) or any other question reserved in paragraph 19.

22.	Plaintiff proposes that the Court obtain a written statement from Magistrate Judge Davis, the relevant records, or both, through a procedure within the Court’s authority, and that the Court set a date for the submission and a period for the parties’ responses. Rule 43(c) permits the Court to hear a motion on affidavits. Plaintiff does not request a deposition of any judicial officer. Plaintiff does not request general financial discovery, unrelated investment records, or any inquiry into judicial deliberations. Plaintiff does not request that nonresponse be treated as establishing ownership.

23.	Obtaining information from Magistrate Judge Davis is not returning adjudication to him. The restored request is to be decided by the assigned magistrate judge.

VI.	RELATED PROCEEDINGS

24.	ECF No. 99 requested that the District Judge determine the historical financial-interest facts in resolving ECF No. 93. Plaintiff maintains that application and the pending objections. Through this Motion, Plaintiff now additionally requests that the assigned successor magistrate judge vacate ECF No. 96, restore the historical component of ECF No. 86, and adjudicate ownership and the statutory character of the reported interest on September 9 and October 7, 2026.

25.	The requested determination would supply a factual record for the District Judge’s consideration of the pending statutory challenge and retrospective relief. This Motion does not ask the successor magistrate judge to decide ECF No. 93 or resolve the objections pending before the District Judge. It asks the successor magistrate judge to decide the restored request in ECF No. 86. Plaintiff seeks a determination of the historical facts, not another reservation of those facts for possible later determination. ECF No. 93, ECF Nos. 89–91, and ECF Nos. 97–99 remain pending before the District Judge. This Motion does not withdraw them, does not transfer them, and does not extend or restart any period to object under Rule 72(a).

26.	This Motion does not request vacatur of ECF No. 64 or ECF No. 84. It does not request that ECF No. 59-1 become the operative pleading. It does not request adjudication of any Defendant’s liability on the underlying claims. Its object is ECF No. 96 and the request ECF No. 96 left undetermined.

VII.	RELIEF REQUESTED

27.	Plaintiff requests an order, in the form of Proposed Order A or, in the alternative, Proposed Order B:

First, vacating ECF No. 96;

Second, restoring for decision the historical financial-interest component of ECF No. 86 identified in Part V and Request A2, as to September 9, 2026 and October 7, 2026;

Third, entering the findings stated in paragraph 17;

Fourth, in the alternative, determining on the record whether the asset reported as “FB common stock” was owned on each of those dates by Magistrate Judge Davis individually or as a fiduciary, by his spouse, or by a minor child residing in his household, and whether the interest on each date was a financial interest within § 455(d)(4), after the factual development described in paragraphs 21 and 22 and an opportunity for the parties to address the resulting record;

Fifth, if the record shows ownership on either date by a holder described in § 455(b)(4) other than Magistrate Judge Davis individually, entering that finding in place of findings (b) and (c);

Sixth, recognizing that further prospective relief against Magistrate Judge Davis under ECF No. 86, Requests A1, A3, and A4, is unnecessary following reassignment, without that recognition disposing of the historical request; and

Seventh, stating the disposition of the vacatur request, the requested ownership findings, and the alternative request for factual development and determination; and, for any request not reached, identifying the ground on which the Court declines to reach it.

28.	Plaintiff submits with this Motion the Memorandum in Support, Proposed Order A, and Proposed Order B. Plaintiff relies on the existing record, including ECF Nos. 64, 84, 86, 86-1 through 86-3, 87, 93, 96, 97, and 99, and the October 22, 2026 reassignment entry. No new declaration accompanies this Motion.

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff respectfully requests that the Court enter Proposed Order A or, in the alternative, Proposed Order B.
